# GitHub Actions Workflows

| File | Purpose | Triggers |
|------|---------|---------|
| `ci.yml` | Test → Build Docker image → Vulnerability scan | Every push and PR |
| `terraform-checks.yml` | Terraform fmt + validate status checks | Push/PR touching `terraform/**` |

---

## ci.yml — Application CI

This workflow enforces a strict gate order: tests must pass before the image is built, and the image must be built before it is scanned.

### Jobs

```
test ──► build ──► scan
```

### 1. Test

Runs the full Jest suite against Node.js 20. All downstream jobs are skipped if any test fails.

| Step | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| Checkout | Fetches the repository at the triggering ref |
| Set up Node.js | Installs Node 20; restores the npm cache between runs |
| Install dependencies | `npm ci` — clean, reproducible install from `package-lock.json` |
| Run tests | `npm test` — executes Jest; the job fails if any test fails |

### 2. Build Docker image

Runs only after **Test** passes. Builds the image and exports it as a tarball artifact so the **Scan** job can load it without needing a container registry.

| Step | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| Checkout | Fetches the repository |
| Set up Docker Buildx | Enables BuildKit for multi-platform and cache support |
| Extract metadata | Generates image tags and OCI labels automatically (see [Tags](#tags)) |
| Build image and export to tar | Builds the image and writes it to `/tmp/image.tar` |
| Upload image tarball | Saves the tar as a GitHub Actions artifact (retained for 1 day) |

#### Tags

Tags are generated by [`docker/metadata-action`](https://github.com/docker/metadata-action):

| Condition | Tag produced |
|-----------|-------------|
| Any push or PR | `sha-<short-commit-sha>` |
| Push to any branch | `<branch-name>` |
| Pull request | `pr-<pr-number>` |
| Push to `main` only | `latest` |

### 3. Image vulnerability scan

Runs only after **Build** passes. Downloads the tarball artifact, loads it into the Docker daemon, and scans it with [Trivy](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-action).

| Step | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| Download image tarball | Fetches the artifact produced by the Build job |
| Load image | `docker load` — makes the image available to Trivy by name |
| Trivy scan (table) | Prints a human-readable findings table in the job log; never fails the job |
| Trivy scan (SARIF) | Writes `trivy-results.sarif`; **fails the job** if any unfixed `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` CVE is found |
| Upload SARIF | Uploads to the **GitHub Security → Code scanning** tab (runs even if the scan step failed) |

#### Scan configuration

| Setting | Value | Reason |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `severity` | `CRITICAL,HIGH` | Focuses on actionable, high-impact findings |
| `ignore-unfixed` | `true` | Suppresses CVEs with no available fix to reduce noise |
| `vuln-type` | `os,library` | Covers both OS packages and language-ecosystem dependencies |
| `exit-code` on SARIF step | `1` | Fails the pipeline when fixable critical/high vulnerabilities are present |

#### Viewing results

- **Job log** — the table scan step prints a quick summary inline.
- **GitHub Security tab** — navigate to *Security → Code scanning alerts* to browse findings, filter by severity, and track remediation over time.

#### Layer caching

`cache-from` and `cache-to` both use `type=gha`, storing Docker layer cache in GitHub Actions Cache.

#### Permissions

The **Scan** job sets `security-events: write` (required to upload SARIF). All other jobs use default read-only permissions.

---

## terraform-checks.yml — Terraform status checks

Runs as a required status check on any push or PR that touches files under `terraform/`. Does **not** run on unrelated changes (e.g. application code changes don't trigger this workflow).

### Trigger path filter

```yaml
paths:
  - "terraform/**"
```

### Jobs

```
fmt ──► validate-apps
    └──► validate-pipeline
```

The two validate jobs run in **parallel** after `fmt` passes.

### 1. fmt

| Step | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| Checkout | Fetches the repository |
| Set up Terraform | Installs Terraform 1.9.8 via `hashicorp/setup-terraform` |
| Check formatting | `terraform fmt -check -recursive -diff terraform/` — scans all modules in one pass; prints a diff and exits non-zero if any file is not canonical |

A formatting failure means the author needs to run `terraform fmt -recursive terraform/` locally and push the corrected files.

### 2. validate-apps / validate-pipeline

Both jobs follow the same pattern, each targeting their respective module directory.

| Step | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| Checkout | Fetches the repository |
| Set up Terraform | Installs Terraform 1.9.8 |
| Init (no backend) | `terraform init -backend=false` — downloads providers without touching remote state |
| Validate | `terraform validate` — type-checks the configuration; catches missing required arguments, wrong attribute types, and undefined references |

`-backend=false` means no AWS credentials, Fastly API keys, or remote state config are needed in CI — the check is purely structural.

### Making it a required status check

In the GitHub repository settings (*Settings → Branches → Branch protection rules*), add the following as required status checks on the `main` branch:

- `Format check (terraform fmt)`
- `Validate terraform/apps`
- `Validate terraform/pipeline`

With this in place, no PR can be merged unless all three checks pass.

---

## Extending the workflows

### Add `terraform/modules` or other new module directories

Add a new validate job to `terraform-checks.yml` following the same pattern as `validate-apps`:

```yaml
validate-modules-foo:
  name: Validate terraform/modules/foo
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  needs: fmt
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
      with:
        terraform_version: "1.9.8"
    - run: terraform init -backend=false
      working-directory: terraform/modules/foo
    - run: terraform validate
      working-directory: terraform/modules/foo
```

### Push Docker image to a container registry

Add a `push` job to `ci.yml` after the **scan** job. See the inline comments in `ci.yml` for details.

### Scan a published image instead of a tarball

Point Trivy directly at the registry reference and remove the artifact download/load steps:

```yaml
image-ref: "ghcr.io/<owner>/gists-api-server:${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }}"
```

### Widen Trivy severity threshold

To also catch `MEDIUM` vulnerabilities:

```yaml
severity: "CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM"
```
